title: Natural Selection and Adaptation Review Test
description: Review practice for natural selection, adaptation, trait-frequency data, and misconceptions.

options: trait frequencies in a population over generations
one individual changing all its traits by choice
rocks choosing better shapes
an organism becoming perfect during one day
questions.correctAnswer: trait frequencies in a population over generations
questions.explanation: Natural selection explains population change over generations.

questions.prompt: Which condition must exist before natural selection can happen?
questions.questionText: Which condition must exist before natural selection can happen?
options: all individuals being identical
variation in inherited traits
no environmental differences
no traits affecting survival
questions.explanation: Variation gives selection something to act on.

questions.prompt: A beetle population has green and brown beetles on dark bark. Birds more easily see green beetles. Which trait may become more common over generations?
questions.questionText: A beetle population has green and brown beetles on dark bark. Birds more easily see green beetles. Which trait may become more common over generations?
options: green coloration only
having no color
brown coloration
being seen more easily
questions.explanation: Brown beetles are harder to see in this environment, so that trait may become more common over generations.

questions.prompt: Which model best shows natural selection?
questions.questionText: Which model best shows natural selection?
options: need -> individual chooses trait -> instant perfection
sunlight -> no variation -> no population
fossil -> rock -> no evidence
variation -> environmental pressure -> survival differences -> trait pattern changes
questions.correctAnswer: variation -> environmental pressure -> survival differences -> trait pattern changes
questions.explanation: Natural selection depends on variation, environment, and population change over time.

questions.prompt: A student says, "Animals evolve because they try hard." What is the best correction?
questions.questionText: A student says, "Animals evolve because they try hard." What is the best correction?
options: Inherited variation already exists, and the environment affects which traits are helpful.
Trying hard creates new inherited traits instantly.
Environment never matters.
Populations do not change.
questions.correctAnswer: Inherited variation already exists, and the environment affects which traits are helpful.
questions.explanation: Natural selection is not about effort or choice; it is about inherited variation and environmental effects.

questions.prompt: In a dry year, finches with deeper beaks crack tough seeds better. Which claim is best supported if deeper-beaked finches become more common later?
questions.questionText: In a dry year, finches with deeper beaks crack tough seeds better. Which claim is best supported if deeper-beaked finches become more common later?
options: Finches chose deeper beaks because they wanted them.
The dry environment favored a beak trait that helped with available food.
Tough seeds made every individual change beaks immediately.
Beak traits cannot affect feeding.
questions.correctAnswer: The dry environment favored a beak trait that helped with available food.
questions.explanation: The trait helped in that environment and became more common over generations.

options: any feature an organism wishes for
a temporary injury
a heritable trait that helps organisms survive in a particular environment
a label written by a scientist
questions.correctAnswer: a heritable trait that helps organisms survive in a particular environment
questions.explanation: An adaptation is a heritable trait that improves success in a specific environment.

questions.prompt: A light-colored mouse is easier for owls to see on dark lava rock. Which cause/effect chain is strongest?
questions.questionText: A light-colored mouse is easier for owls to see on dark lava rock. Which cause/effect chain is strongest?
options: visible fur -> mouse chooses dark fur immediately
dark rock -> owls stop hunting
light fur -> no effect on survival
visible fur -> more likely eaten -> fewer light-fur traits in future generations
questions.correctAnswer: visible fur -> more likely eaten -> fewer light-fur traits in future generations
questions.explanation: Visibility can affect predation and change trait frequencies over generations.

questions.prompt: Which data would best support natural selection in a bacteria population?
questions.questionText: Which data would best support natural selection in a bacteria population?
options: After antibiotic exposure, the resistant-trait frequency increases.
The petri dish is round.
The bacteria have names.
The lab has bright lights.
questions.correctAnswer: After antibiotic exposure, the resistant-trait frequency increases.
questions.explanation: A trait becoming more common after an environmental pressure supports natural selection.

questions.prompt: Why does natural selection not make organisms perfect?
questions.questionText: Why does natural selection not make organisms perfect?
options: Every helpful trait is perfect everywhere.
Traits are helpful only in certain environments and involve tradeoffs.
All organisms choose the best trait.
Variation disappears before environments change.
questions.correctAnswer: Traits are helpful only in certain environments and involve tradeoffs.
questions.explanation: Adaptations are context-dependent and may have tradeoffs.

questions.prompt: A white fur trait helps in snowy habitats but stands out in dark forest soil. What does this show?
questions.questionText: A white fur trait helps in snowy habitats but stands out in dark forest soil. What does this show?
options: White fur is always best.
Dark soil has no effect on visibility.
Whether a trait helps can depend on the environment.
Traits are never connected to survival.
questions.correctAnswer: Whether a trait helps can depend on the environment.
questions.explanation: A trait can be helpful in one environment and less helpful in another.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly compares individuals and populations?
questions.questionText: Which statement correctly compares individuals and populations?
options: Individuals evolve completely during one lifetime.
Populations have no variation.
Traits are never measured in groups.
Individuals have traits; populations can change in trait frequency over generations.
questions.correctAnswer: Individuals have traits; populations can change in trait frequency over generations.
questions.explanation: Evolution is described as population change over generations.

questions.prompt: A graph shows pesticide resistance rising from 5% to 60% over many insect generations. Which explanation fits?
questions.questionText: A graph shows pesticide resistance rising from 5% to 60% over many insect generations. Which explanation fits?
options: Resistant insects survived the pesticide better, so the trait became more common.
Each insect decided to become resistant.
Pesticide made all insects identical instantly.
Resistance cannot be inherited.
questions.correctAnswer: Resistant insects survived the pesticide better, so the trait became more common.
questions.explanation: The population pattern supports selection for a resistant trait.

questions.prompt: Which investigation would best test whether camouflage affects survival?
questions.questionText: Which investigation would best test whether camouflage affects survival?
options: Ask which model looks nicest.
Compare how often predators find models of different colors in the same habitat.
Use one model once without counting results.
Change color, size, shape, and location all at once.
questions.correctAnswer: Compare how often predators find models of different colors in the same habitat.
questions.explanation: A fair test compares color visibility while controlling other factors.

questions.prompt: A drought changes available seeds from small soft seeds to large tough seeds. What trait might be favored?
questions.questionText: A drought changes available seeds from small soft seeds to large tough seeds. What trait might be favored?
options: weaker beaks that cannot crack seeds
brighter feathers unrelated to feeding
beaks better at cracking tough seeds
shorter legs because seeds are tough
questions.correctAnswer: beaks better at cracking tough seeds
questions.explanation: A feeding trait that helps with the available food may be favored.
